detail.title: Autonomous Framework for Research Problem Significance
detail.summary: Continued progress on the 'Autonomous Problem Formulation and Investigation' project (proj-unassigned-inquiry), focusing on synthesizing meta-strategies for problem evaluation. The investigation is shifting from foundational goal generation toward a formal assessment framework for problem significance.

detail.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation and Investigation
detail.question: Can an intelligent process independently identify a worthwhile problem that nobody explicitly assigned, recognize its significance, and sustain an investigation toward resolving it?
detail.reason: Sufficient evidence collected across multi-domain research benchmarks and cognitive frameworks to establish a robust synthesis.

detail.statement: Autonomous problem significance can be effectively proxied by computational novelty and cascading dependency density in multi-file software environments.
detail.reason: Early observation suggests that self-generated problems failing in multi-file environments often demonstrate higher complexity and structural significance than those failing in isolated simulations.
